clue.text: Respond to appeal, and discharge

definitions.meaning: in cricket, an umpire answers an appeal from the fielders by declaring the batsman dismissed
to emit or release, as a pipe or a chimney emits fumes

explanation.surface: Someone answers a plea for help and hands over goods or money.
explanation.walkthrough: The appeal is a cricketing one: when fielders shout 'Howzat?', the umpire's positive answer is to raise a finger and dismiss the batsman.
explanation.definitionFit: An umpire who upholds an appeal rules the batsman dismissed, and to emit something is a second sense of the phrasal verb.

clue.text: Soldier capturing a coarse Italian leader

indicators.note: capturing says the soldier's letters surround the pieces after it

parts.note: GI is an American soldier
ribald means coarse or vulgar

explanation.surface: A soldier arrests a vulgar Italian commander.
explanation.walkthrough: Giuseppe Garibaldi led the struggle for Italian unification in the 19th century.
explanation.definitionFit: Garibaldi was the military leader of the Italian Risorgimento.

clue.text: With rapidly changing pitch, six bowled at Oval without a run

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the run stands on the outside of the letters of 'at Oval'

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals
B is the cricket abbreviation for bowled
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run
taken as written
O is oval in shape

explanation.surface: A cricket report: a batsman is bowled for six at the Oval without scoring a run.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is cricket (the Oval is a London Test ground), but 'pitch' is musical. 'without' is used in its old sense of outside: R stands outside AT O.
explanation.definitionFit: Vibrato is a pulsating effect in singing or playing produced by small rapid variations in pitch.

clue.text: Cricket side, those people conclude, is improving

parts.note: the on side is the leg side of a cricket field
them refers to those people
to end is to conclude

explanation.surface: A cricket team's finish suggests its form is getting better.
explanation.walkthrough: The ON side (also called leg side) is the half of a cricket field behind the batsman's legs.
explanation.definitionFit: Recovering from illness or setback means getting better.

clue.text: Heavy work, as far as I am concerned

definitions.text: as far as I am concerned
definitions.meaning: the two-word phrase meaning 'in my opinion'

explanation.surface: Someone finds a task burdensome, at least in their own view.
explanation.definitionFit: A tome is a big heavy volume, and split in two it reads as the phrase 'in my view'.

clue.text: Staff whip wild animal

parts.note: a staff is a long pole
the cat (cat-o'-nine-tails) is a whip

explanation.surface: Someone with a stick and a lash goes after a wild beast.
explanation.definitionFit: The polecat is a wild mammal of the weasel family.

clue.text: Political positions shared by callers

definitions.meaning: the official policies of a political party
telephone lines used by several subscribers at once

explanation.surface: Party policy is agreed among people on the phone.
explanation.definitionFit: A party's policies are its official stances, and a shared telephone connection is a second meaning.

clue.text: Tenure lecturer initially obtained with no difficulty

indicators.note: initially says only the first letter of lecturer is used

parts.note: ease is freedom from difficulty

explanation.surface: A lecturer secures a permanent post without any trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: A lease is a contract granting tenure of property for a set term.

clue.text: Jazz centre, fashionable in the past

parts.note: chic means stylish or fashionable
ago means in the past

explanation.surface: A jazz club that used to be trendy.
explanation.definitionFit: The city was a major hub of early jazz in the 1920s.

clue.text: Trains on this for a lot of athletic events

definitions.meaning: the rails that railway trains run on
running races as opposed to field events

explanation.surface: An athlete trains here for many competitions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trains' looks like a verb for an athlete practising; it is the railway noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Railway rails are laid along a permanent way, and running races are grouped as one class of athletics.

clue.text: Turn back as transport runs in the other direction

indicators.note: in the other direction says the pieces before it are read from right to left

parts.note: the Tube, London's underground railway, is a form of transport
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A traveller turns round because the trains are heading the wrong way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the other direction' turns TUBER round. 'Turn back' as in repel an attack or rebuff a charge.
explanation.definitionFit: To rebut is to repel or refute, driving an argument or attack back.

clue.text: Female's cocktail

definitions.meaning: a woman's given name; the 's stands for 'is'
a mixed drink of tequila, lime and orange liqueur

explanation.surface: A woman's favourite mixed drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Female's' as 'Female is': the first definition is a woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Margarita is a girl's name and also a tequila-based mixed drink served in a salt-rimmed glass.

clue.text: Lab equipment schoolmaster used with hesitation

parts.note: beak is old British school slang for a schoolmaster (also a magistrate)
er is the sound of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: A teacher stammers while handling apparatus in the science lab.
explanation.definitionFit: A beaker is a lipped glass vessel used in laboratories.

clue.text: Doctor's replacement meets explorer in London area

parts.note: Mr Hyde is the form that takes the place of Dr Jekyll in Stevenson's story
Mungo Park was a Scottish explorer of the Niger

explanation.surface: A locum doctor and a traveller meet up somewhere in London.
explanation.walkthrough: HYDE PARK is a large royal park in central London.
explanation.definitionFit: The royal park is a well-known open space in central London.

clue.text: Ignorant, like soldiers, about opponent of West

indicators.note: about says the soldiers' word goes round the piece after it

parts.note: soldiers are dressed in uniform
in bridge, North and South play against East and West, so N opposes West

explanation.surface: Soldiers are mocked as know-nothings when facing a western enemy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opponent of West' looks like East, but in bridge North is West's opponent too.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone lacking knowledge or information is ignorant.

clue.text: Not bound to be so immoral

explanation.surface: Someone free of obligation is assumed to be wicked.
explanation.definitionFit: Untied things are free, and a person of lax morals is called that too.

clue.text: Be rough in reshuffle, as PM is to Chancellor

indicators.note: a reshuffle rearranges, so the letters of the words before it are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A Prime Minister is told to be tough when reorganising the Cabinet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reshuffle' rearranges BE ROUGH IN. The Prime Minister lives at 10 Downing Street and the Chancellor of the Exchequer next door at No 11.
explanation.definitionFit: The two ministers live in adjoining houses in Downing Street, so each is the other's next-door resident.

clue.text: Courage one English naval commander reported to another

indicators.note: reported says the commander's name is spoken and spelt by its sound

parts.note: Thomas Hardy was Nelson's flag captain at Trafalgar
Samuel Hood was another British admiral

explanation.surface: One English admiral speaks of the bravery of a fellow officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reported' turns HARDY into its sound-alike HARDI.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardihood is boldness or daring.

clue.text: Raised gun to kill soldiers or majestic creature

indicators.note: Raised in a down clue says the pieces are read from bottom to top

parts.note: a gat is slang for a gun
to slay is to kill
OR stands for other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Soldiers raise their guns to shoot, or to bring down a fine beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raised' turns GAT SLAY OR upwards. A royal stag is a red deer with at least twelve points on its antlers.
explanation.definitionFit: A royal stag is a red deer with a large set of antlers, a noble animal.

clue.text: Naughty child pronounced you stupid? What cheek!

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child

indicators.note: pronounced says the phrase before it is spoken, and the letters entered match the sound

parts.note: 'you dense' means 'you stupid'

explanation.surface: An exasperated adult calls a cheeky brat stupid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pronounced' signals that 'you dense', said out loud, gives UDENCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Impudence is cheek, insolent disrespect.

clue.text: Theatrical character I included in special report

indicators.note: included in says the letter I goes inside the rearranged word
special suggests a reworked version, so the letters of report are rearranged

explanation.surface: A theatre figure appears in a one-off feature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'special' rearranges REPORT into PERROT, and 'included in' sets I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Pierrot is the sad white-faced clown of French pantomime.

clue.text: Willing to study a year

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it

explanation.surface: A student is keen to spend a year on their studies.
explanation.definitionFit: Ready means prepared or willing to do something.

clue.text: For example, protected by very sharp weapon

indicators.note: protected by says the piece before it sits inside the word for very

parts.note: assai is the musical term for very

explanation.surface: An example of a well-guarded, very sharp weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: ASSAI, very, appears in tempo markings such as allegro assai.
explanation.definitionFit: An assegai is a slender iron-tipped spear of southern Africa.

clue.text: What correspondents may need is in iron case

parts.note: to press clothes is to iron them
a box is a case or container

explanation.surface: Something journalists require is kept in a metal container.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'correspondents' are reporters, not letter-writers.
explanation.definitionFit: A press box is the area reserved for reporters at a sports ground.

clue.text: It needs copy to fill page, right?

definitions.text: It needs copy to fill page, right?

indicators.note: to fill says the piece before it goes inside the pieces after it

parts.note: to ape is to copy

explanation.surface: An editor checks that copy will fill the page.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines a newspaper, which needs journalists' copy to fill its pages.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper must have written material to fill every page before it is printed.

clue.text: Thoroughly clean foreign coin in acid

indicators.note: in says the coin's letter goes inside the word for acid

parts.note: sour means acid in taste
C is the abbreviation for cent, a coin of the USA and other countries

explanation.surface: A foreign coin is cleaned by soaking it in acid.
explanation.definitionFit: To scour is to scrub thoroughly.

clue.text: Train passes on Eastern line

parts.note: to pass on is to die

explanation.surface: A train goes by on a railway line in the east.
explanation.definitionFit: A diesel is a train hauled by a diesel engine.

clue.text: Language used by Monsieur Dumas

indicators.note: used by says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Which tongue did the French novelist Dumas speak?
explanation.definitionFit: Urdu is the national language of Pakistan.

clue.text: Actor in cast taken in by monarch

indicators.note: taken in says the word before it is held inside the pieces that follow

parts.note: per means by, as in 'per post'
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen
a cast is a form or mould

explanation.surface: An actor in the company is welcomed by the Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Actor in cast' reads as a theatre phrase, but 'in' is only a link and 'cast' means a mould, not a company of players.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor is one who performs on stage.

clue.text: Letters coming before I break out — it may signify nothing

definitions.text: Letters coming before I break out
definitions.meaning: the word that opens the question '___ I break out?', asking whether one should escape
a variant of 'aught' or 'nought', meaning zero

explanation.surface: A prisoner wonders whether to escape, though the thought may come to nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The first part is a fill-in-the-blank: the letters that come before 'I break out' to make a question. Ought and aught are old words for nought, a zero.
explanation.definitionFit: Ought is an old variant of nought, a zero, and it is the modal verb that starts a question about obligation.

clue.text: No longer involved with Labour, red flag included

indicators.note: included says the word before it is held inside the word red

parts.note: taken as written
to flag is to tire

explanation.surface: Someone has left the Labour Party, red banner and all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour' looks like the political party, but here it means work: the definition is someone who has stopped working.
explanation.definitionFit: A retired person has given up paid work.

clue.text: Ruin a French performance

parts.note: un is French for a
a doing is a performance, as in 'that took some doing'

explanation.surface: A French show is a disaster.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's undoing is their downfall or ruin.
